title: Polynomial tests for universal power lifting with nil kernel
statement: Let $u:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. For $n\geq0$, let $u_n:R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to S[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ apply $u$ to coefficients, using [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Suppose every element of $\ker u$ is nilpotent, and for every $n\geq0$ and every $b\in S[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ there exist $N>0$ and $a\in R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ such that $u_n(a)=b^N$. Then for every commutative $R$-algebra $E$, the map $u_E:E\to E\otimes_R S$, $e\mapsto e\otimes1$, has elementwise nilpotent kernel, and every $z\in E\otimes_R S$ has a positive power $z^M$ in its image. The tensor product is scalar extension [def-weil-module-base-change], with multiplication $(e\otimes s)(e'\otimes s')=ee'\otimes ss'$. No characteristic, finiteness, flatness or reducedness hypothesis is imposed; in particular $\ker u\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q=0$ is not required.

source.place: Remark 3.2.2, printed p.496 (polynomial tests), Lemma 3.1.4, printed p.495, and the spectral part of the proof of Proposition 3.3.5, printed p.498 (nil kernel under base change). The conclusion only retains nil kernels and power lifting, not the characteristic-zero clause of an adequate homeomorphism. Published primary PDF https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Take $n=0$. By [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] the zero-variable polynomial rings are $R$ and $S$, so every $s\in S$ has a positive power in $u(R)$. Together with the assumed elementwise nilpotent kernel, these are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-pur-all-element-powers-spectrum-homeomorphism]. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is a homeomorphism, in particular surjective.

Fix a commutative $R$-algebra $E$. Put $D=E\otimes_R S$ and $g:E\to D$, $g(e)=e\otimes1$. Its commutative ring structure and the maps $g$ and $j:S\to D$, $j(s)=1\otimes s$, are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property](1). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spec-surjective-base-change] to the surjection from step 1 and the ring map $R\to E$: the induced map $\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}E$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 00FI, lemma-surjective-spec-radical-ideal, final base-change assertion; tensor ring structure from Section 00CV

proof.text: If $e\in\ker g$ and $\mathfrak p$ is any prime ideal of $E$, step 2 gives a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $D$ with $g^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$. Since $g(e)=0\in\mathfrak q$, we have $e\in\mathfrak p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq], applied to the zero ideal, $e\in\bigcap_{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}E}\mathfrak p=\sqrt{(0)}$. Thus $e^k=0$ for some $k\geq1$. This is elementwise nilpotence; it does not require a single exponent for the whole kernel.

source.place: Tag 00E0, lemma-Zariski-topology, item (7) and the definition of the radical

proof.text: For $z\in D$, tensor-product generation in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] writes $z=\sum_{i=1}^m e_i\otimes s_i$, absorbing $R$-scalar coefficients into $e_i$. Put $b=\sum_i s_it_i\in S[t_1,\ldots,t_m]$. The hypothesis gives $N>0$ and $a\in R[t_1,\ldots,t_m]$ with $u_m(a)=b^N$. By [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], evaluate $S[t_1,\ldots,t_m]\to D$ by $s\mapsto j(s)$ and $t_i\mapsto g(e_i)$. The tensor multiplication from [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property](1) sends $b$ to $\sum_i(1\otimes s_i)(e_i\otimes1)=z$. Evaluation sends $u_m(a)$ to $g(a(e_1,\ldots,e_m))$: on a coefficient $r$, $j(u(r))=1\otimes u(r)=r_E\otimes1=g(r_E)$ by balancing, and both maps send $t_i$ to $g(e_i)$. Polynomial uniqueness therefore identifies these maps. Preservation of powers gives $z^N=g(a(e_1,\ldots,e_m))$. If the sum is empty, $z=0$ and $N=1$, $a=0$ work. This proves power lifting for every $E$.
